body: PAIRING LEAD: Treat phone/tablet pairing as a device-authorization transaction, never as sharing the presenter session. Existing authenticated console creates 128-bit CSPRNG pair_id, single-use, 90s TTL; QR appears ONLY on private console and contains no access/refresh token. New device must authenticate, scan/enter code, then both devices display the same short-authentication string and the existing console explicitly approves device name + requested scopes. Rate-limit code attempts per transaction/IP/account and kill after 5 failures; responses must not reveal valid/invalid session membership. Approval atomically consumes pair_id and creates a NEW opaque, server-side, presentation-scoped device session in __Host- Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie. Default scopes console:read + card:publish only if explicitly requested; never tenant/admin/corpus privileges. Rotate on approval/role change; revoke on session end, unpair, logout, expiry; list active devices with revoke control. WebSocket topics are assigned server-side from the device principal; no arbitrary room IDs. Reauthorize every command and periodically revalidate long-lived connections. Never put credentials in URL/query/log/localStorage; never use a QR bearer token. RFC 8628 specifically requires high-entropy device codes, short expiry, rate limiting, polling limits, and user-code confirmation; RFC 9700 requires audience restriction and replay defenses. Sources: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628.html ; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/WebSocket_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html
